title: Matthew Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Matthew 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with 'The book of the generation of Jesus Christ' which indicates that He is mentioned first.

questions.question: Who begat Isaac?
questions.explanation: The text states 'Abraham begat Isaac' clearly indicating Abraham is the father of Isaac.

questions.question: Who is the son of David mentioned in Matthew 1?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Jesus Christ, the son of David,' indicating that Jesus is the son of David.

questions.question: Who begat Phares and Zara?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states 'And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar,' indicating Thamar as their mother.

questions.question: Who is the father of Solomon?
questions.explanation: The text states 'And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon,' indicating David as Solomon's father.

questions.question: Who begat Aram?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'and Esrom begat Aram,' indicating Esrom as the father of Aram.

questions.question: Who begat Booz?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab,' indicating Salmon as Booz's father.

questions.question: Who is mentioned as the king in Matthew 1?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'And Jesse begat David the king,' clearly identifying David as a king.

questions.question: Who begat Josaphat?
questions.explanation: The text states 'And Asa begat Josaphat,' indicating Asa as the father of Josaphat.

questions.question: Who was the wife of Urias?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias,' directly referring to Bathsheba.

questions.question: Who begat Joram?
questions.explanation: The text states 'And Josaphat begat Joram,' indicating Josaphat as the father of Joram.

questions.question: Did Abraham begat Jacob?
questions.explanation: The text states 'Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob,' confirming that Abraham is indeed the grandfather of Jacob.

questions.question: Did Solomon begat Roboam?
questions.explanation: The text states 'And Solomon begat Roboam,' confirming that Solomon is the father of Roboam.

questions.question: Did Ozias begat Solomon?
questions.explanation: The text does not say 'Ozias begat Solomon'; instead, it states 'And Joram begat Ozias,' which is different.

questions.question: Did Jesse begat Solomon?
questions.explanation: The text states that Jesse begat David, who then begat Solomon, meaning Jesse is not the direct father of Solomon.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Matthew 1:10, who was the father of Josias?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:10 states that Manasses begat Amon, and Amon begat Josias, making Amon the father of Josias.

questions.question: What does Matthew 1:11 promise will happen if someone is carried away to Babylon as stated in Matthew 1:10?
options: They will still be part of the genealogy leading to Christ
They will lose their place in the genealogy
They will be forgotten by God
questions.correctAnswer: They will still be part of the genealogy leading to Christ
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:11 mentions Josias and his brethren were carried away to Babylon, and the genealogy continues through Jechonias, showing God's plan continues despite exile.

questions.question: Who is the husband of Mary according to Matthew 1:16?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:16 clearly states that Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, who gave birth to Jesus.

questions.question: How does Matthew 1:12 relate to Matthew 1:11 in the genealogy?
options: Jechonias begat Salathiel after the Babylonian captivity
Josias begat Jechonias before the captivity
Salathiel was carried away to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Jechonias begat Salathiel after the Babylonian captivity
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:11 mentions the carrying away to Babylon and 1:12 continues by stating after being brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel, showing continuity despite exile.

questions.question: What practical lesson about God's faithfulness can be learned from the continuation of the genealogy through the Babylonian exile?
options: God's promises remain true despite difficult circumstances
God abandons His people in exile
Only those born in the homeland are blessed
questions.correctAnswer: God's promises remain true despite difficult circumstances
questions.explanation: The genealogy continues through exile (Matthew 1:11-12) demonstrating God's unchanging faithfulness even in hardship.

questions.question: According to Matthew 1:17, how many generations were there from Abraham to David?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:17 states explicitly that from Abraham to David are fourteen generations.

questions.question: How can understanding the structured genealogy in Matthew 1:17 encourage a Christian's faith journey?
options: It shows God's order and timing in fulfilling promises
It proves only certain people are chosen
It discourages trust in God's plan
It focuses only on past generations
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's order and timing in fulfilling promises
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:17 reveals God's deliberate plan in history, encouraging believers to trust His timing and faithfulness.

questions.question: What does Matthew 1:18 reveal about Mary's state before she and Joseph came together?
options: She was found with child of the Holy Ghost
She was not espoused to Joseph
She was married to another man
questions.correctAnswer: She was found with child of the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:18 states Mary was espoused to Joseph but before they came together, she was found with child by the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: How can Christians apply the truth of Matthew 1:18 about Jesus' birth to their understanding of faith and obedience?
options: Trust in God's miraculous work even when circumstances seem uncertain
Only follow God when everything is clear
Doubt God's plan if it seems unusual
Ignore God's involvement in difficult situations
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God's miraculous work even when circumstances seem uncertain
questions.explanation: The miraculous conception (Matthew 1:18) teaches believers to trust God's power and plan beyond human understanding.

questions.question: According to Matthew 1:13, who was the father of Eliakim?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:13 states that Zorobabel begat Abiud, and Abiud begat Eliakim, making Abiud the father of Eliakim.

questions.question: How does the genealogy in Matthew 1:13-14 demonstrate God's providence in the lineage of Christ?
options: It shows a continuous and deliberate line despite historical challenges
It shows many broken and unconnected lines
It emphasizes only the kings of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a continuous and deliberate line despite historical challenges
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:13-14 continues the genealogy smoothly through many generations, showing God's providence in preserving the messianic line.

questions.question: Who begat Matthan according to Matthew 1:15?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:15 states Eliud begat Eleazar; Eleazar begat Matthan, making Eleazar the father of Matthan.

questions.question: What practical lesson about legacy and faithfulness can be drawn from the detailed genealogy in Matthew 1:10-16?
options: Being faithful in small steps contributes to God's greater plan
Only kings' lives matter in God's plan
Faithfulness is only for the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: Being faithful in small steps contributes to God's greater plan
questions.explanation: The genealogy includes many individuals, showing that each generation's faithfulness is part of God's unfolding plan (Matthew 1:10-16).

questions.question: What does the genealogy in Matthew 1 emphasize about God's plan for Jesus' birth?
options: It was a fulfillment of divine promise through generations
It was a sudden surprise without history
questions.correctAnswer: It was a fulfillment of divine promise through generations
questions.explanation: Matthew 1 shows Jesus' birth as the culmination of God's promise through a well-documented lineage.

questions.question: Jesus is called Christ according to Matthew 1:16.
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:16 explicitly states Jesus is called Christ.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 1.

questions.question: What did Joseph consider doing when he learned of Mary's condition?
questions.explanation: Joseph, being a just man, was minded to put her away privily (Matthew 1:19).

questions.question: Who appeared to Joseph in a dream?
questions.explanation: The angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream (Matthew 1:20).

questions.question: What name was Joseph instructed to call Mary's son?
questions.explanation: The angel told Joseph to call his name JESUS (Matthew 1:21).

questions.question: What prophecy does Matthew cite regarding a virgin?
options: She shall bring forth a son
questions.correctAnswer: She shall bring forth a son
questions.explanation: The prophecy states that a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son (Matthew 1:23).

questions.question: What did Joseph do after waking from sleep?
questions.explanation: Joseph did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him and took unto him his wife (Matthew 1:24).

questions.question: What does the term 'firstborn' refer to in the context of Jesus?
questions.explanation: 'Firstborn' indicates that Jesus was the first child born to Mary (Matthew 1:25).

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'JESUS' in Matthew 1:21 mean?
questions.explanation: The name JESUS comes from the Hebrew 'Yeshua', meaning 'God saves' (Matthew 1:21).

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Matthew 1:22-23 when referencing the prophecy?
questions.explanation: The verses exemplify typology by connecting the birth of Jesus to Old Testament prophecy of a virgin (Matthew 1:22-23).

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy is echoed in Matthew 1:22-23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:22-23 fulfills the prophecy of Isaiah 7:14 regarding a virgin bearing a son.

questions.question: What comes before Matthew 1:20?
options: Joseph's consideration to put Mary away
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph's consideration to put Mary away
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:19 discusses Joseph's thoughts before the angel's appearance in Matthew 1:20.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'angelos' mean in Matthew 1:20?
questions.explanation: 'Angelos' translates to 'messenger', indicating the role of the being who spoke to Joseph (Matthew 1:20).

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew 1:1-17?
questions.explanation: The genealogy frames Jesus’s lineage from Abraham to David to emphasize fulfillment of promise (Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.question: The statement 'she was found with child of the Holy Ghost' is a fulfillment of what?
questions.explanation: This statement directly references the fulfillment of the prophecy given in Isaiah regarding the virgin birth (Matthew 1:18).

questions.question: True or False: Joseph was initially willing to publicly disgrace Mary.
questions.explanation: Joseph was not willing to make her a public example (Matthew 1:19).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus means 'God saves'.
questions.explanation: The name JESUS means 'God saves', as stated in Matthew 1:21.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 1:18 teach about the nature of Jesus' conception?
options: Jesus was conceived by the Holy Ghost, affirming His divine origin
Jesus was conceived by Joseph and Mary naturally
Jesus' conception was a mythological story
Jesus was adopted at birth and later recognized as divine
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus was conceived by the Holy Ghost, affirming His divine origin
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:18 states that Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost, teaching the doctrine of the virgin birth and divine conception.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 1:21 teach about the purpose of Jesus' coming?
options: Jesus came to save His people from their sins
Jesus came primarily to establish an earthly kingdom
Jesus came to abolish the law and prophets
Jesus came to bring political freedom to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus came to save His people from their sins
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:21 explicitly states that Jesus shall save His people from their sins, affirming the doctrine of salvation through Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding God's covenant faithfulness is taught by Matthew 1:1?
options: Jesus is the son of David and Abraham, showing God's ongoing covenant with His people
Jesus is unrelated to Old Testament promises
God's covenant ended before Jesus' time
Jesus represents a new covenant unrelated to Abraham or David
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the son of David and Abraham, showing God's ongoing covenant with His people
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:1 identifies Jesus as son of David and Abraham, affirming God's covenant faithfulness through the promises made to both patriarchs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 1:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 1:20, the angel reveals to Joseph in a dream what he ought to do, demonstrating God's omniscience in knowing and guiding human affairs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Matthew 1:22 by fulfillment of prophecy?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:22 notes that these events happened to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet, demonstrating God's sovereign control over history.

questions.question: How does Matthew 1:17 connect to the broader biblical narrative regarding God's plan of salvation?
options: It structures the genealogy to highlight God's orderly plan through history in three sets of fourteen generations
It ignores the Old Testament background
It emphasizes human effort over divine intervention
It shows a random list of ancestors without theological meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It structures the genealogy to highlight God's orderly plan through history in three sets of fourteen generations
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:17 divides the genealogy into three groups of fourteen, reflecting God's providential orchestration of salvation history.

questions.question: In what way does Matthew 1:23 narratively fulfill Old Testament prophecy?
options: It fulfills Isaiah's prophecy of a virgin birth and the name Emmanuel meaning 'God with us'
It contradicts all Old Testament prophecies
It presents a new prophecy unrelated to previous Scriptures
It refers to a symbolic rather than literal fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Isaiah's prophecy of a virgin birth and the name Emmanuel meaning 'God with us'
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:23 explicitly cites Isaiah's prophecy, showing Jesus' birth as fulfillment of God's promise of divine presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 1:6 and Matthew 1:16 teach about Jesus' human and royal lineage?
options: Jesus is both a descendant of King David and the legal son of Joseph, establishing his Messianic claim
Jesus is descended only from Joseph without any royal ancestry
Jesus' lineage excludes David to avoid political implications
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is both a descendant of King David and the legal son of Joseph, establishing his Messianic claim
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:6 traces Jesus' ancestry to King David and 1:16 mentions Joseph, affirming Jesus' legal and royal heritage necessary for Messianic fulfillment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 1:19 and Matthew 1:20 teach about Joseph's righteousness and God's intervention?
options: Joseph's just nature leads him to mercy, and divine revelation redirects his action to fulfill God's plan
Joseph ignores God's will and acts harshly
Joseph acts impulsively without divine guidance
Joseph's righteousness causes him to reject Mary permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph's just nature leads him to mercy, and divine revelation redirects his action to fulfill God's plan
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph's righteousness in not wanting to disgrace Mary, and 1:20 shows God intervening through an angel to guide him, combining human virtue and divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 1:24 and Matthew 1:25 teach about obedience and marital sanctity in the incarnation narrative?
options: Joseph's obedience to God's command and the sanctity of marriage prior to Jesus' birth
Joseph rejects Mary after the angel's message
Marriage is irrelevant to Jesus' incarnation
Joseph publicly accuses Mary of adultery
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph's obedience to God's command and the sanctity of marriage prior to Jesus' birth
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:24-25 show Joseph obeying the angel and taking Mary as wife, respecting marital sanctity even before Jesus' birth, highlighting divine-human cooperation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Matthew 1:18-25 teaches an improbable story of virgin birth and divine intervention. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The passage affirms the miraculous conception of Jesus by the Holy Ghost and God's sovereign guidance through Joseph
The passage teaches Jesus was conceived naturally and Joseph was deceived
The passage is purely symbolic and not meant to be historical
The passage denies Jesus' divine origin
questions.correctAnswer: The passage affirms the miraculous conception of Jesus by the Holy Ghost and God's sovereign guidance through Joseph
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:18-25 clearly teach the doctrine of the virgin birth and divine intervention in Joseph's decision, affirming Jesus' divine origin and God's providential plan.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding God's providence is taught in Matthew 1:11 in the context of Israel's exile?
options: God's plan includes the exile to Babylon as part of redemptive history
Exile is a random event unrelated to God's plan
The exile nullifies God's covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God's plan includes the exile to Babylon as part of redemptive history
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:11 refers to Jechonias and brethren being carried to Babylon, showing God's providential use of exile in His salvation plan.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Matthew 1:5 by including Gentile women like Rachab and Ruth in Jesus' genealogy?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:5 includes Gentile women, illustrating God's grace extending salvation beyond Israel's ethnic boundaries.

questions.question: How does the genealogy in Matthew 1:12-16 prepare for the Messianic mission of Jesus in the New Testament?
options: It traces Jesus' lineage through the post-exilic community, emphasizing restoration and continuity
It breaks the line of David intentionally
It omits key ancestors to obscure Jesus' identity
It focuses only on Joseph's ancestry
questions.correctAnswer: It traces Jesus' lineage through the post-exilic community, emphasizing restoration and continuity
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:12-16 covers the period after Babylonian exile, showing God's continued covenant work culminating in Jesus' mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 1:23 and Matthew 1:21 teach about Jesus' identity and mission?
options: Jesus is Emmanuel, 'God with us', and He saves His people from their sins
Jesus is only a political leader without divine identity
Jesus' mission excludes salvation from sin
Jesus' name is unrelated to His mission
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is Emmanuel, 'God with us', and He saves His people from their sins
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:23 affirms Jesus as 'God with us,' and 1:21 explains His saving mission, together revealing His divine nature and redemptive purpose.
